name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network and dirt ground tiles, flat ground texture seen from above

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tileset sheet (256 wide, 192 rows) showing asphalt road pieces (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, a large fill block) on a dirt background. Everything is drawn flat top-down with no standing volume. The silhouette is a full-width 256 rectangle and the column scans show only texture variation (aggregate, cracks, patches), with no front-edge line, eave shadow or front face. As a ground terrain tile, a flat top-down look is the expected representation, so there is no vertical front face to measure.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has two materials, a brown dirt field and blue-grey asphalt. Each reads as only about 3 lightness steps, against the reference paving at about 6-7. Only 12 distinct colours exist in total, and the 5 visible tones per tile sit between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is low at 4%, so the surfaces are not flat fills, but the speckle is sparse and repetitive. The dirt is mottled with blotches and the asphalt has faint hairline cracks. The road edge is a darker, tinted lip with no neutral black outline (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), which fits the material-tone approach. The crumbling edges and chunks do read, and the crossroads and dead ends are laid out correctly. The patch, oil stain and long cracks are barely visible at this scale, though, and the ramps are shallower than the Beodeul 5-6 step standard. When in doubt, fail.
